assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening of a new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice that identified a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, then tied neutrinos to a blazar flare (TXS 0506+056), to NGC 1068 and to the Galactic plane. This is instrument-driven discovery with clear originality and large lasting impact on cosmic-ray origin and multi-messenger astronomy. From an experimental astroparticle perspective this is the sort of detector-led result the prize has rewarded.
assessment.attribution: Only one credited name is supplied. Halzen conceived and led IceCube and is a defensible single laureate on the supplied credit, but a large collaboration and key early proposers and instrument builders are not in the credited list, so a single-name configuration may look narrow and could draw attribution objections.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the diffuse flux has been confirmed by several analyses and independent channels, and the source associations have grown over a decade. Some source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are at moderate significance and the origin of most of the flux remains open, but the core discovery is firm and the timing is good.
uncertainties: Single credited name may not capture the full set of decisive contributors.
Source-population origin of most neutrinos is still unresolved.
I am relying on my own recollection of significances and have not verified them here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, enabling relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a path to redefining the second. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye demonstrated the best-performing strontium clocks. The importance, originality and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Katori (concept, magic wavelength) and Ye (record accuracy and clock comparisons) are the two clearest decisive contributors in the supplied credit. Pairing them is natural and avoids ambiguity with the earlier comb prize; other clock groups (e.g. ion-clock work) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent clocks at several national laboratories agree at the 10^-18 level, and applications in geodesy and dark-matter searches are established. Recognition is timely; the redefinition of the second is still pending but not required.
uncertainties: Overlap in public perception with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes could dilute novelty.
Other groups may deserve credit that this two-name list does not carry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made superconducting qubits controllable and readable through microwave photons, underpinning the leading solid-state quantum computing platforms. Importance and lasting impact are high and the concept (strong coupling of an artificial atom to a resonator) is clean.
assessment.attribution: Four names are credited and the limit is three. Blais (with Girvin) proposed the theory, Wallraff and Schoelkopf realised strong coupling in 2004. I would choose the two experimental leaders and the principal theory proposer, which leaves Girvin out and is a genuine unresolved allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the laboratory sense, with broad independent replication, though it follows closely on the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so the timing question is whether the committee wants to return to the area so soon.
uncertainties: Close adjacency to the most recent superconducting-circuit award.
Credit between Blais and Girvin is hard to separate; omitting one is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray, then optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts located their hosts and redshifts and settled their cosmological origin after decades of debate. A decisive, instrument-enabled observational discovery with lasting impact on high-energy astrophysics. It is also close to my own field of gamma-ray and X-ray instrumentation, so I weigh it with some awareness of that proximity.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray instruments (Costa, Frontera and colleagues) provided the arcminute localisation, and Kulkarni's group delivered optical and radio follow-up and redshifts. The supplied names can support a three-person prize, but others, including deceased pioneers and collaborators, are not available, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly three decades of confirmation and a very well understood physical picture, with later missions building on it. Recognition could be seen as late, but that does not weaken the case.
uncertainties: Several key contributors (instrument teams, optical discoverers) may fall outside the three-name limit or the credited list.
Astrophysics-versus-physics balance in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays found a correlated nanohertz signal consistent with a gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries. This opens a new gravitational-wave band and is conceptually striking.
assessment.attribution: The result is from three regional collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA). The credited names map to each, but the discovery was collective and the individual decisive contributions are difficult to assign to three people.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view: the Hellings-Downs correlation is at roughly 2 to 4 sigma in the individual arrays, the astrophysical origin is not settled, and no independent detection above the conventional 5 sigma threshold exists in the supplied evidence. I would watch this candidate for later years.
uncertainties: Significance below the discovery threshold in my recollection; not verified here.
Origin of the signal (black-hole binaries versus new physics) is open.
Three-name credit does not fit a three-collaboration discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, followed by the HgTe observation, created a vast field of topological quantum matter. Originality and influence are very high and the conceptual story is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group realised the effect in HgTe wells (after Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, who are not credited here); Hasan's observation of 3D topological insulators is a separate part. A compound discovery whose parts need different recognition. I choose the two theorists and the first experimental realisation.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many materials and measurements confirm the picture and the field is long established, though the 2016 prize already recognised topological phases.
uncertainties: Hasan and the uncredited BHZ theorists complicate a clean three-person allocation.
Overlaps with B004 and B037, which I treat as the same broad family.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new class of tunable correlated and superconducting phases, with a prior theoretical flat-band prediction. The impact on condensed matter is large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic-angle flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. This is a clear theory plus experiment pairing, though other experimental groups are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for its age: widely reproduced, but microscopic mechanisms of the superconductivity are still debated and the field is developing, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of superconductivity not settled.
Other experimental groups (e.g. those who observed related effects) are outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision measurements of CMB anisotropies that fixed cosmological parameters and established the standard model of cosmology. Importance is high, and as a space instrument it is of particular interest to me.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was the instrument and optics lead, and Spergel the key analysis and parameters figure. The credited trio is a reasonable configuration, but the cosmology prize in 2006 for COBE and 2019 for cosmology complicate novelty, and many team members contributed.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed by Planck, but recognition now might be seen as redundant given earlier CMB-related prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and later cosmology prizes.
Large-collaboration attribution is hard to compress to three.
